materials.name: Fujii A cotton plain sheeting — measured specimen

structure.specimen: A in Tables 1 and 3; commercial cotton plain sheeting, not a generic cotton law
structure.finish: No dyeing, coating or other post-processing
structure.composition_scope: Source identifies commercial cotton fabric; no independent composition assay reported
structure.cotton_count_notation: Table 1: / denotes a single yarn; // denotes two parallel single yarns of equal cotton count
structure.conditioning: All specimen tests: JIS L0105; 20 +/- 2 degrees C; 65 +/- 4 percent RH
structure.weight_scope: Table 1 omits the Weight unit; five 5 x 5 cm2 specimens averaged. No mass or areal density is inferred
structure.tensile_protocol: Appendix C.1: JIS L1096 A strip test; Shimadzu AG-100kNX; 50 mm width; 200 mm gauge; 100 mm/min until rupture; five specimens per direction
structure.tensile_fit_model: Eq (17): E(e)=d*ln((b+exp(a*e))/(b+1))+c*e+d*(1-exp(-k*e)) for e>=0; k=a*sqrt(b)/(b+1); odd continuation for e<0. E is stress in Pa, not a constant modulus; e is engineering strain
structure.tensile_summary_scope: Appendix C.1 p20: elastic is the fitted stress-response derivative as strain tends to infinity; low is that derivative at strain corresponding to 500 gf/cm tensile load per width, not the zero-strain slope
structure.poisson_fit_model: Eq (19): nu_hat(e)=b*e^c*exp(a*e)+d for e>=0; video extensometry from five tensile specimens per direction. Eq (42) corrects initial apparent ratios to satisfy reciprocity using elastic, not low, tensile moduli
structure.shear_fit_model: Eq (18): G(g)=a*ln(1+b*g)+c*g+d*(1-exp(-k*g)) for g>=0; k=sqrt(-a*b*b/d); odd continuation for g<0; g is shear angle in radians. Source extrapolates beyond its measured 8-degree range; no extrapolated law is activated
structure.mechanical_scope: Only thickness and source-interval membrane shear slope are canonical mechanical properties; original fujii_* fit coefficients remain unconsumed extensions
structure.bending_scope: Reported B_KES in Pa only: Eq (44) prints strain=z*kappa*10^2 but labels z in mm and kappa in cm^-1, which would require 10^-1. No canonical bending rigidity is inferred from this dimensional ambiguity; twisting was not measured
structure.data_scope: Published summary values and fitted coefficients; no raw replicates or uncertainty distributions ingested
structure.rights: Fujii et al. (2026), CC BY 4.0; numerical transcription with stated unit conversions

thickness.method: Table 1 p6; KES-FB3-A; mean of 25 readings, five tests on each of five specimens
